item.title: Man accused in Cornell case allegedly asked student not to "say anything," transcript says
item.description: According to the record, a student who had been at the Chi Phi house the night of the alleged assault told a Title IX investigator she got a call the next day from one of the accused men.

item.title: Trump vows Iran war to end "very quickly" as more troops head to Mideast
item.description: Some 9,000 more U.S. forces head for the Middle East as Trump vows the war will end "right after the election," if not sooner.

item.title: N.Y. AG appointed as special prosecutor in Cornell alleged rape case
item.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James will serve as special prosecutor in the Cornell University alleged rape case.

item.title: DOE employee arrested by FBI for allegedly trying to support Houthis in Yemen
item.description: A Department of Energy electrical engineer has been arrested on charges of providing support to the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels.

item.title: Patient dies by suicide after "insurance issue" delayed medicine
item.description: Hours after experiencing a flare-up related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, Kenney Blewett of Kyle, Texas, died by suicide in June.

item.title: Trump says Iran "ready to fold up"
item.description: Trump said he doesn't believe "you could ever have peace" with Iran, and renewed his threat to resume U.S. attacks after the midterms.

item.title: Divers locate final body from the Catalina Island helicopter crash
item.description: Three people died and two more were hospitalized after a medical helicopter crashed off the coast of Catalina Island.

item.title: Cornell Title IX investigation docs reveal new details on rape investigation
item.description: CBS News has examined hundreds of pages of transcripts obtained by CBS News New York of the Title IX investigation conducted by Cornell University into the allegations made by a former student who claims she was drugged and gang-raped at a fraternity house.

item.title: How a small Outer Banks community rescued a young couple's wedding day from a storm
item.description: Kimberly and Jayden Sink were preparing for their dream destination wedding on North Carolina's Hatteras Island, until a nor'easter got in the way. Then something unexpected happened.

item.title: Rick Ross accused of strangling, hitting woman in Miami Beach
item.description: Rapper Rick Ross was arrested by Miami Beach police Thursday on felony battery by strangulation and misdemeanor battery charges involving domestic violence.

item.title: Crew docks at space station with astronaut who'll miss birth of 3rd child
item.description: With the arrival of four fresh space station crew members, four others will head for home after 235 days in orbit.

item.title: $1.7 million raised in scheme for Hamas, including from U.S. donors, feds say
item.description: Saleem Alzaq, a 45-year-old Gaza man who prosecutors allege is a longtime Hamas member, was charged with helping operate the fundraising campaign claiming to provide humanitarian aid, according to an indictment.

item.title: Bee & Co. skincare store at Westfield Topanga closes after sales tactic allegations
item.description: The closure comes after months of reporting from CBS California Investigates on allegations that Bee & Co. employees targeted vulnerable shoppers and pressured them into purchasing expensive skin care products and devices.

item.title: Jane Doe's account of what happened at Cornell fraternity house
item.description: A former Cornell student, identified as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit against the school and seven former fraternity brothers she accuses of rape and sexual assault.

item.title: SpaceX Crew 13 docking at International Space Station
item.description: A multi-national crew of four is arriving at the International Space Station for a six-month mission aboard the orbiting lab. They took off on Thursday morning and SpaceX Crew 13 is in the process of docking Thursday night. CBS News space consultant Bill Harwood has more about the process.

item.title: Attorney on Christa Pike's botched execution: "The real issue here is that we don't know anything"
item.description: Death row inmate Christa Pike was scheduled to die by lethal injection on Wednesday night in Tennessee, but the procedure failed and she is still alive. Her attorneys say she is in critical condition and is receiving life-saving medical care. Bo King, the attorney for Brad Sigmon, who was executed by firing squad, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Astronaut aboard SpaceX rocket has pregnant wife at home: "Making a sacrifice"
item.description: Two hundred and sixty miles above the Earth, the Dragon spacecraft is set to reach the International Space Station for a six-month stay. It has four astronauts on board, including one with another big mission back on Earth. Mark Strassmann has the story.

item.title: Trump likely to pick Jay Clayton for AI czar, sources say
item.description: Jay Clayton will likely be the White House's pick for AI czar, and the Trump administration has been discussing having him remain in his current role as director of national intelligence, according to sources briefed on the matter.

item.title: Homan defends ICE crackdown: "Give me an example of where we went too far"
item.description: As the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration draws pushback from some GOP lawmakers, White House border czar Tom Homan told CBS News critics should "educate themselves."

item.title: Tennessee cancels executions after Christa Pike survives botched injection
item.description: Tennessee canceled its remaining scheduled execution this year after Christa Pike, the only woman on its death row, survived two doses of a botched lethal injection. A witness said she was "clearly very alive."

item.title: Christa Pike's attorneys: Botched execution was "torturous" and "predictable"
item.description: Attorneys for Christa Pike, who survived an attempt by the state of Tennessee to put her to death, say they warned that her execution could be botched in exactly the way it was.

item.title: Man accused of planning deadly Texas State Capitol attack, DPS says
item.description: Texas DPS said Benny Caldera Jr., 40, was arrested at his home in Bexar County.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: California governor nominees Becerra and Hilton face off in fiery debate
item.description: California gubernatorial nominees Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton faced off in a heated CNN debate on Wednesday with just over a month to go before the midterm elections. CBS News' Zak Hudak has more.

item.title: More details emerge about FlyDubai co-pilot who tried to crash plane
item.description: Questions about the motive of the co-pilot who tried to crash a packed flight from Dubai to Israel continue to swirl.

item.title: 10/1: CBS Evening News
item.description: New video revealed of FlyDubai incident; Jane Doe said she felt "like bait," docs reveal.

item.title: Man who allegedly harassed Katie Miller indicted for cyberstalking in Massachusetts
item.description: The man allegedly contacted Katie Miller by phone and text over 40 times in around two months and left "disturbing messages about the victim and her husband," the Justice Department said.

item.title: 10/1: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump says he's campaigning in Republican strongholds "just to make sure"; Homan asked about ICE killing of Renee Good.

item.title: How some AI models are more vulnerable to manipulation
item.description: China has embraced open-weight models, a development that researchers say is closing the AI capability gap between the country and the U.S.

item.title: Cyber scams have targeted 9 in 10 Americans as AI fuels fraud
item.description: Cyberattacks and scams are skyrocketing due to artificial intelligence, which is making it easier for criminals to engage in fraud, the report finds.
